analyst_note: Hormuz Day 66; Naval Blockade Day 23; Project Freedom Day 2; WPA Day 6 Past Statutory Deadline. Project Freedom's opening night produced the most significant direct US-Iran kinetic exchange of the conflict: by the close of Day 1 operations on May 4, CENTCOM confirmed US forces destroyed six Iranian small boats and intercepted Iranian cruise missiles and combat drones — and issued an explicit, unambiguous statement that 'no US Navy ships have been struck.' The two American-flagged merchant vessels that transited the strait under US military cover on Day 1 are confirmed successes, but a retired Lieutenant General framed it correctly: a tactical success measured against 120 vessels per day pre-war is not a restored strait. Iran is not backing down — its forces fired cruise missiles, rockets, and combat drones near commercial and military vessels throughout Day 1, confirming that the kinetic exchange phase of the Hormuz conflict has begun in earnest. The morning opens on Day 2 with the operation active, both sides having exchanged fire, no US casualties confirmed, and commercial traffic still a fraction of pre-war levels. That equilibrium — Iranian harassment without US ship losses — is the de-escalation scenario; it is also fragile. Breaking Defense analysts said Day 1 results were consistent with Project Freedom being 'unlikely to pay off right away,' a judgment the commercial shipping market appears to share: the strait remains almost empty of non-US commercial traffic. On the economic front, ADP weekly data for the period ending April 11 showed a sharp deceleration — average of 39,250 jobs per week, down from 54,750 the prior four-week period — a significant leading-indicator softening ahead of Friday's April jobs report. On the institutional front, the DOJ's decision to drop its investigation of Jerome Powell clears the last structural obstacle to Kevin Warsh's confirmation: Senator Tillis dropped his hold, and the full Senate floor vote is now clear for the week of May 11, before Powell's May 15 expiry. Iranian cyber retaliation risk remains elevated through the 72-hour post-Project Freedom window; no updated CISA advisory has been issued. PNW: 459 Northwest communities rated at higher wildfire risk than previously assessed by new modeling tools; PNW remains dry through at least May 6, with NOAA projecting hot, dry conditions through July. Vibe 3.

vibe.rationale: Vibe 3. A fractional upgrade from yesterday's 2, calibrated narrowly on the fact that Project Freedom's opening day did not produce the worst-case scenario: CENTCOM confirmed no US Navy ships were struck, 6 Iranian small boats were destroyed, cruise missiles and combat drones were intercepted, and two American-flagged merchant vessels transited successfully. The catastrophic escalation scenario — a US warship hit by Iranian fire, direct naval war, oil spike to $130+ — did not occur on Day 1. That shifts the probability-weighted outlook from 'imminent escalation to direct war' to 'active but contested naval campaign.' The vibe is 3 rather than 5 because: the kinetic exchange is real and ongoing; Iran fired cruise missiles and drones in Day 1; Iranian boats were destroyed; the diplomatic track (14-point proposal via Pakistan) faces its greatest credibility test as the military operation deepens; commercial shipping has not returned to anything approaching normal volumes; Breaking Defense analysts expect Project Freedom to take time with uncertain success; Iranian cyber retaliation risk is at its peak 72-hour window; and the structural economic and domestic stressors are unchanged. The marginal improvement from a 2 is the confirmation that the war has not immediately escalated to a phase involving US naval casualties — a scenario that was the morning's primary risk on May 4. That single factor — the crisis didn't immediately get catastrophically worse — is the delta.

geopolitical.summary: Hormuz Day 66; Naval Blockade Day 23; Project Freedom Day 2. CENTCOM confirmed that by the end of Day 1 operations (May 4), US forces destroyed six Iranian small boats and intercepted cruise missiles and combat drones. No US Navy ships were struck. Two American-flagged merchant vessels transited the strait under US military cover — the first successful commercial transits since the closure began February 28. Iran fired cruise missiles, rockets, and combat drones near commercial and military vessels throughout Day 1. Analysts characterize Day 1 as a 'tactical success' that must be measured against the pre-war flow of 120 vessels per day. Commercial traffic from non-US operators remains negligible — Iran's threat posture is successfully sustaining the perception of risk that keeps most shippers away. The 14-point diplomatic proposal via Pakistan nominally remains active; Trump said US representatives have had 'very positive discussions' with Iran. Day 2 opens with both sides having exchanged fire, the operation continuing, and the fundamental binary unresolved: can Project Freedom restore commercial volume to a threshold that meaningfully changes Iran's leverage position?

items.headline: Project Freedom Day 1 Close: US Destroys 6 Iranian Small Boats, Intercepts Missiles/Drones; No US Ships Struck; Two Transits Confirmed
items.summary: CENTCOM confirmed the Day 1 results of Project Freedom by Monday evening: US forces destroyed six Iranian small boats that posed a threat to the operation's corridor; US military assets intercepted Iranian cruise missiles and combat drones launched toward commercial and military vessels in the strait; and the command statement explicitly confirmed 'No US Navy ships have been struck.' The two American-flagged merchant vessels that transited the Strait of Hormuz under US military cover represent the first successful commercial transits since Iran closed the strait February 28. The US force package — 15,000 personnel, two aircraft carriers, Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers, AH-64 Apache and MH-60 helicopters, F-15s, F-16s, F-35s, EA-18G Growlers, drones, and a mapped narrow safe corridor — functioned as designed on Day 1 of contested operations. The operational posture is a 'guide' model rather than a direct naval escort: US forces mapped a corridor and provided aviation and maritime cover, but warships are not physically sailing alongside merchant vessels. Breaking Defense reporting noted that analysts expect Project Freedom to take time to pay off, and the commercial shipping market appears to share that assessment — non-US commercial traffic through the strait remains near zero, as Iran's sustained threat posture is sufficient to keep most operators away regardless of the US military corridor's existence. Retired Lt Gen Karen Gibson characterized Day 1 as a tactical success that must be measured against 120 vessels per day — the pre-war baseline the strait must approach to meaningfully change Iran's strategic position.

items.headline: Iran Fires Cruise Missiles, Rockets, and Drones in Day 1 Response; 'Will Not Back Down'; Strait Still Nearly Empty of Commercial Traffic
items.summary: Iran's Day 1 response to Project Freedom confirmed that Iranian forces are willing to engage US military and commercial assets with cruise missiles, rockets, and combat drones when the operation is active. Iranian forces fired at commercial and military vessels in the strait throughout May 4; the US military's interception of those munitions represents active air defense operations in a contested combat environment. Iranian parliamentary and military leadership reiterated that Iran 'will not back down' from its Hormuz posture — a position unchanged since February 28. The strait's commercial traffic situation as of Day 1's close remains effectively unchanged: the two US-flagged transits are confirmed, but non-US commercial shipping operators are not following. Iran's harassment campaign — even when partially intercepted by US forces — is sufficient to sustain the perception of risk that keeps operators from routing through the strait on commercial terms. The operation's strategic success depends not on whether US-flagged ships can transit (they can, with US military coverage), but on whether the broader commercial market assesses Project Freedom's protection umbrella as sufficient to resume normal routing — a judgment that Day 1's hostile Iranian response makes significantly harder.
actors: Lloyd's of London war risk analysts

items.headline: Pakistan Back-Channel 14-Point Proposal: Nominally Active Under Military Pressure; Day 2 Diplomatic Signal Watch
items.summary: The Iran 14-point proposal — delivered via Pakistan back-channel May 2, reviewed by Iran as of May 3 per Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei, characterized by Trump on May 4 as subject to 'very positive discussions' — enters Day 2 under its most significant stress test since delivery. Iran's Day 1 military response (missile/drone launches, boat confrontations) and the US military's Day 1 kinetic response (six Iranian boats destroyed, munitions intercepted) are occurring on the same day that Trump publicly claimed 'very positive discussions.' The diplomatic track's credibility depends on an Iranian Foreign Ministry signal today that the military operations track has not foreclosed negotiation. If Iran issues a statement on May 5 that the 14-point proposal remains viable despite Day 1 kinetics, the dual-track (military pressure + diplomatic channel) hypothesis holds; if Iran declares the diplomatic track dead in response to Day 1 US military actions, the conflict enters a phase where no off-ramp is publicly available. The sequencing deadlock — Iran defers nuclear talks; US requires nuclear commitment upfront — remains unresolved regardless of the kinetic track's outcome.

economic.summary: ADP's weekly employment data for the four weeks ending April 11 showed a sharp deceleration — average of 39,250 jobs per week — down from 54,750 per week in the prior four-week period ending April 4. The April rate equates to approximately 157,000 jobs per month, near the low end of consensus estimates (150-165K) for the May 8 BLS Employment Situation report. The Fed's own assessment is that official payrolls are overstating job growth by approximately 60,000 per month — which, if accurate, would place the real April gain below 100,000. Oil prices and equities are responding in real time to Project Freedom's Day 1 results; the commodity market's verdict on Day 2 will be shaped by whether additional commercial operators attempt the corridor. The structural inflation picture — PCE at 3.5%, household tariff cost $1,500/year, JPMorgan projecting 80% tariff pass-through to consumers in H2 2026 — is unchanged and compounds with the Hormuz energy shock. GDP growth for 2026 is tracking at approximately 2.1%, reflecting resilience against the structural drag.

items.headline: ADP Weekly Data Shows Sharp April Deceleration: 39,250 Jobs/Week (Apr 11 Period) vs. 54,750 (Apr 4 Period); May 8 BLS Report Risk Elevated
items.summary: ADP's National Employment Report weekly pulse data for the four weeks ending April 11, 2026 showed US private employers added an average of 39,250 jobs per week — a significant deceleration from the 54,750 per week average for the four weeks ending April 4. The April 11 pace annualizes to approximately 157,000 jobs per month — near the low end of the BLS April consensus range of 150-165K. The deceleration is concentrated in mid-April, following the first full month of tariff pass-through effects, Hormuz disruption, and federal workforce contraction. The Fed's own internal assessment — that official payroll figures are overstating job growth by approximately 60,000 per month due to birth-death model and seasonal adjustment methodology — introduces a risk that the 'real' April gain could be below 100,000 jobs, a figure that would materially alter Warsh's first FOMC policy calculus. Initial jobless claims (Thursday May 7) and the full ADP report (Wednesday May 7) are the pre-BLS leading indicators to watch; a claims number above 230K or ADP below 130K would sharpen the downside risk framing for Friday. Markets are priced for a near-consensus result — a significant miss would reprice rate cut expectations.

items.headline: Project Freedom Day 2 Oil/Equity Pricing: Market Verdict on Day 1 Kinetics Emerges; Gas at $4.46/Gallon (AAA), 50% Above Pre-War
items.summary: Financial markets on Day 2 (May 5) are pricing Project Freedom's Day 1 kinetic outcome: US forces destroyed six Iranian small boats and intercepted cruise missiles and drones; no US ships struck; two merchant transits completed. This outcome is better than the worst-case but falls far short of the strait-reopening scenario that would drive oil materially lower. Markets are likely to sustain a risk-premium posture — oil elevated relative to pre-war levels, equities subdued — until commercial traffic volumes through the strait increase meaningfully beyond the two Day 1 transits. AAA reported national average gas at $4.46/gallon on May 4, 50% above the pre-war $2.98/gallon baseline from February 28. Every additional week of Hormuz closure compounds the structural energy-inflation input into the PCE trajectory. The April 8 week-over-week surge in the 4-week ADP average (54,750/week) suggests early April optimism that Project Freedom or diplomatic resolution was imminent; the April 11 deceleration to 39,250/week suggests that optimism was not sustained in hiring decisions. The tariff pass-through trajectory — JPMorgan projecting 80% consumer cost shift in H2 2026 — is now overlapping with the Hormuz energy shock and the deceleration in labor market momentum.

items.headline: Warsh Path Clears: DOJ Drops Powell Investigation; Tillis Drops Hold; Full Senate Vote Week of May 11 Now Unobstructed
items.summary: The Department of Justice has dropped its investigation into Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell — the factor that had given Senator Thom Tillis (R-NC) grounds to place a hold on Kevin Warsh's Senate confirmation. With the DOJ dropping the investigation, Tillis confirmed he has dropped his hold. The Senate Banking Committee advanced Warsh's nomination on April 29 on a 13-11 party-line vote; Warsh's full Senate confirmation is now targeted for the week of May 11, before Powell's term expires May 15. Powell confirmed he will remain on the Fed Board of Governors after stepping down as chair — an institutional continuity signal. The 53-seat Republican caucus plus Senator Fetterman (D-PA)'s signaled yes vote provides a comfortable margin absent Republican defections. The elimination of the DOJ-hold obstacle removes the last major structural risk to a pre-May 15 Warsh confirmation, preserving the institutional transition timeline. Warsh would assume the chairmanship in a stagflation environment — PCE at 3.5%, labor market decelerating, Hormuz energy shock — with his first FOMC meeting targeted for June 16-17.

infrastructure.summary: Iranian cyber retaliation risk remains at peak elevation through the 72-hour post-Project Freedom window (through approximately May 7). No updated CISA advisory has been issued since AA26-097A (April 7). The Stryker Corporation cyberattack — claimed by Handala, a pro-Iranian group, in March 2026 — provides the most significant new reference point for Iranian-affiliated cyber capability: destructive malware wiped more than 200,000 devices across 79 countries, forcing operational shutdowns across global healthcare delivery. FINRA issued a sector-specific cybersecurity alert on heightened Iranian cyber threats in the financial sector. The 6 Iranian small boats destroyed and munitions intercepted in Day 1 operations represent direct kinetic provocation that historically drives Iranian cyber units to escalate parallel asymmetric operations against US civilian infrastructure. PNW grid stress continues from post-heat-wave hydro compression and below-normal snowpack; above-normal temperatures forecast through the week of May 11 extend the cooling load demand on a hydro-constrained system.

items.headline: 72-Hour Peak Cyber Retaliation Window Active Through May 7; No Updated CISA Advisory; FINRA Issues Financial Sector Alert
items.summary: CISA advisory AA26-097A (April 7) documented that Iranian-affiliated APT groups have conducted a sustained campaign against programmable logic controllers across US water, energy, and government OT/ICS systems since at least March 2026, with confirmed operational disruptions and financial losses at victim facilities. The IRGC cyber doctrine of coupling kinetic military escalations with parallel PLC attacks on US civilian infrastructure makes the 72 hours following Project Freedom's launch — through approximately May 7 — the peak cyber retaliation risk window of the conflict to date. No updated CISA advisory has been issued since April 7. FINRA issued a sector-specific cybersecurity alert in April on heightened threats from Iranian cyber actors to the financial sector, extending the threat advisory surface beyond the water, energy, and government sectors documented in AA26-097A. Operators of US water utility SCADA systems, energy sector distribution and generation OT environments, financial sector trading infrastructure, and government facility control systems should treat this 72-hour window as the highest-risk cyber period of the conflict. The six Iranian boats destroyed by US forces in Day 1 represent a kinetic trigger that Iranian cyber planners may use to justify escalating from sustained-access operations to higher-impact destructive attacks.

items.headline: Stryker Cyberattack (March 2026): Handala Wipes 200,000+ Devices Across 79 Countries; Healthcare Delivery Disrupted — Benchmark for Iranian Destructive Capability
items.summary: The March 2026 cyberattack on Stryker Corporation — claimed by Handala, a pro-Iranian hacker group — represents the most operationally significant Iranian-affiliated destructive cyber action against US-linked critical infrastructure in the conflict to date. The attack deployed destructive malware that wiped more than 200,000 devices across Stryker's global network in 79 countries, forcing operational shutdowns and directly affecting healthcare delivery. Stryker is a major medical technology company supplying surgical instruments, implants, and hospital infrastructure globally. The attack demonstrated that Iranian-affiliated groups have developed and deployed supply-chain-scale destructive malware against a US-headquartered critical infrastructure operator — not a disruptive PLC manipulation, but a wipe-level destructive payload deployed at global scale. This capability benchmark raises the plausibility of similar destructive attacks against US water, energy, and financial sector infrastructure during the Project Freedom cyber retaliation window. The CISA AA26-097A advisory (April 7) documented sustained PLC exploitation; the Stryker attack demonstrates the groups operating in the same threat landscape are capable of more destructive operations when motivated.

items.headline: PNW Grid: Hydro Compression Continues; Dry Through May 6; Above-Normal Temps Through May 11; NERC Elevated Risk Summer Outlook Active
items.summary: The Pacific Northwest power grid enters May 5 in a structurally stressed condition that compounds across all contributing factors: post-heat-wave soil moisture depletion and snowpack loss are compressing Columbia River hydro generation headroom; above-normal temperatures are forecast to persist through at least the week of May 11, sustaining above-seasonal cooling demand; and NERC's 2026 summer reliability assessment flagged the West at elevated risk of energy emergencies during peak periods. The PNW forecast remains dry through at least May 6, with NOAA projecting a hot, dry May-July period consistent with the La Nina/El Nino transition pattern. Washington State's statewide snowpack sits at 53% of the median as of April 2026 — in the 5th percentile of all years on record, meaning 95% of years have had more snowpack at this point in the season. The spring melt-pulse that sustains summer hydro generation is materially diminished. Iranian cyber retaliation risk against energy sector OT/ICS systems during the 72-hour post-Project Freedom window compounds the physical grid stress with a cyber threat vector operating simultaneously.

domestic.summary: WPA Day 6 past statutory deadline; Project Freedom is on its second operational day with no congressional authorization — the constitutional accountability gap deepens each day. The DOJ's decision to drop its investigation of Jerome Powell cleared the last structural obstacle to Warsh's full Senate confirmation; Tillis's hold is dropped; the floor vote week of May 11 is now unobstructed. The Senate voted along party lines to initiate the $70B ICE/CBP reconciliation process (Reconciliation 2.0); committee submissions are due May 15. Powell will remain on the Fed Board after stepping down as chair on May 15 — an institutional continuity signal. The VRA redistricting operationalization following Louisiana v. Callais (6-3, April 29) continues to accelerate as multiple GOP-led states prepare redistricting maps ahead of the 2026 midterm cycle.

items.headline: WPA Day 6 Past Deadline; Project Freedom Active Day 2 Without Authorization; 6 Iranian Boats Destroyed — Deepest Constitutional Gap of the Conflict
items.summary: As of May 5, Project Freedom — CENTCOM's 15,000-personnel naval escort operation conducting active combat operations in the Strait of Hormuz, having destroyed six Iranian small boats and intercepted cruise missiles and drones on Day 1 — is conducting direct offensive military operations without congressional authorization. The War Powers Resolution 60-day clock expired April 29; the sixth Senate war-powers resolution failed 47-50 (Collins and Paul crossed; Fetterman remained the lone Democratic no). Project Freedom represents a more acute WPA challenge than any prior phase of the conflict: the operation destroyed Iranian military assets in Day 1 combat — an offensive military action that goes beyond presence, deterrence, or economic pressure characterizations available to the administration in prior phases. The administration has not submitted a formal war authorization request. Congressional Democratic objections continue; Republican leadership has not moved to force a vote. The constitutional accountability gap is at its deepest point: direct offensive combat in a contested maritime zone, without authorization, in the seventh day past the statutory deadline.

items.headline: Reconciliation 2.0: Senate Party-Line Vote Initiates $70B ICE/CBP Process; Week of May 11 Is Triple Convergence — Warsh, Reconciliation, Powell Expiry
items.summary: The Senate voted along party lines to initiate budget reconciliation for a $70 billion, three-year Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection funding bill — Reconciliation 2.0. This procedural vote launches the process that is targeted for a House floor vote the week of May 11, compressing three major legislative tracks into a single week: Warsh's full Senate floor confirmation vote (before Powell's May 15 expiry), Reconciliation 2.0 House floor vote, and all committee submissions due May 15. The House's 215-211-1 budget resolution vote — held open more than five hours over E15 ethanol provisions from Midwestern Republicans — previewed the coalition management challenge. Reconciliation 2.0's $70B price tag and three-year timeline will face harder coalition holds than the procedural resolution, particularly from any Republican member with state-level concerns about ICE operations or fiscal cap implications. The Warsh confirmation is now structurally unobstructed following the DOJ dropping the Powell investigation and Tillis dropping his hold; the 53-seat Republican caucus plus Fetterman's signaled yes provides the votes absent defections.

items.headline: VRA Redistricting Operationalization Continues: 15 Black House Seats Vulnerable; Alabama, Georgia, Texas, NC Preparing Maps Ahead of Midterm Lock
items.summary: The Supreme Court's April 29 ruling in Louisiana v. Callais (6-3, Alito) restricting Voting Rights Act Section 2 to intentional discrimination — and striking Louisiana's majority-Black second congressional district — continues to be operationalized by Republican-led states at an accelerating pace. NPR analysis identified at least 15 current Black House members whose seats are vulnerable to GOP redistricting under the new standard. Alabama, Georgia, Texas, and North Carolina are reported to be preparing redistricting challenges. The first-mover advantage is significant: states that file new maps before follow-on litigation clarifies the ruling's scope may lock in electoral gains for the November 2026 midterm cycle. The ACLU and NAACP Legal Defense Fund are preparing counter-litigation, but the judicial timeline for resolution before November 2026 is narrow. The ruling's downstream impact — the first federal election conducted under the new VRA standard — is being actively operationalized, with state-level GOP parties treating the window before midterm cycle map-lock as a strategic asset.

local_pnw.summary: 459 Northwest communities have been rated at higher wildfire risk than previously assessed, according to new modeling published in May 2026 — a significant upward revision to the pre-season risk baseline. PNW remains dry through at least May 6; NOAA is projecting a hot, dry May-July with snowpacks at record lows. Washington State's statewide snowpack sits at 53% of the median (5th percentile of all years on record) — the spring melt-pulse is materially diminished. Early wildfire season onset is projected for Northern California and the PNW from June 2026. Oregon measles cases stand at 20 confirmed as of April 17, with state officials stating they believe cases are significantly underreported. Washington State measles holds at 40 confirmed cases YTD (more than triple full-year 2025).

items.headline: 459 Northwest Communities Upgraded to Higher Wildfire Risk; Early Season June Onset Projected; WA Snowpack at 5th Percentile of All Years on Record
items.summary: New wildfire risk modeling published in May 2026 has elevated 459 Pacific Northwest communities to higher wildfire danger ratings than previously assessed — a significant upward revision to the pre-season risk map. The revision reflects updated exposure modeling incorporating climate-driven fuel dryness, population-in-risk-zone metrics, and updated fire behavior projections under current drought conditions. Separately, the Pacific Northwest is facing an early wildfire season timeline: fire managers project above-normal fire potential east of the Cascades from June 1, with risk expanding west as summer progresses. Washington State's statewide snowpack at 53% of the April median — in the 5th percentile of all years on record — means the spring snowmelt pulse that historically delays vegetation drying and holds ignition risk lower in May-June is materially absent this year. The combination of new community risk exposure data, early-season onset projection, Forest Service PNW staffing below pre-DOGE baselines, and compressed snowmelt establishes a structurally high-risk fire baseline entering the critical June-August window. National Q1 2026 wildfire data (1.6 million acres burned, more than double the 10-year average) set the national backdrop for regional risk assessment.

items.headline: WA Measles: 40 Cases YTD (3x Full-Year 2025); OR Measles: 20 Cases with Significant Suspected Underreporting; National: 1,814 Confirmed
items.summary: Washington State's measles outbreak holds at 40 confirmed cases year-to-date — more than triple the full-year 2025 count of 12 cases — spanning eight counties, with Kittitas County formally in outbreak status. No overnight acceleration has been reported. Oregon's separate measles situation is developing: 20 confirmed cases as of April 17, with Oregon state officials explicitly stating they believe the true case count is significantly higher than confirmed figures, indicating the outbreak is outpacing case-finding capacity. National confirmed US measles cases reached 1,814 as of April 30, 2026 — a significant annual total at less than four months into the year. The structural drivers are unchanged: below-threshold MMR vaccination coverage in affected communities, DOGE-related CDC workforce reductions constraining federal surge capacity, and school-year spread dynamics still in play through late May. The combination of Washington cases (40 confirmed with unknown-source spread) and Oregon cases (20 confirmed with likely significant undercounting) establishes a bi-state PNW measles situation that exceeds prior outbreak thresholds in both states. School dismissal protocols, community vaccination events, and state emergency declaration thresholds are the next-tier watch items as the school year approaches its final weeks.

items.headline: PNW Heat Continues to Recede; Dry Through May 6; Wildfire Pre-Season Fuel Dryness Accumulating Daily Under Above-Normal May Temperatures
items.summary: The Portland-area heat wave that peaked at approximately 92°F on May 3 continues to recede, but the PNW forecast remains dry and above-normal through at least May 6, with NOAA's spring and summer outlook projecting continued hot, dry conditions through July. Each above-normal day in May extracts soil moisture and advances fuel dryness ahead of the June-August peak fire window — a process that 2026's early and intense heat wave is accelerating relative to any historical May baseline. Portland Metro Council's heat season (declared May 1 through September 30) is active, with cooling center protocols available. The fire weather implication of persistent above-normal May temperatures compounding on a 5th-percentile snowpack year is that fuel conditions entering the June onset window will be substantially drier than the 10-year design-basis for Forest Service pre-positioning. NIFC's seasonal outlook projects above-normal fire potential east of the Cascades from June 1 — less than four weeks from today.
